text:
maria_support: FYI ACME reported a sharp p95/p99 jump starting ~02:12 UTC, user-facing 503s and heavy request queuing. They say it started after yesterday's routing tweak. attaching brief repro.

raj_oncall: Looking. Can you paste the customer request IDs or a sample trace? any customer-side spikes?

maria_support: sample request id: req_0a9f3c. Customer says retries spike, logs show 'queueing_delay_ms=1200' then 503. No auth errors. They repro by replaying ~500 rps for 2m against prod token.

liz_runtime: On it — initial glance at runtime metrics shows worker_latency and kv-cache contention on shard-gpu-7. There was an ingress routing change that moved a subset of traffic to lower-capacity pool (priority-tiering rule). Might be colliding with concurrency caps.

tom_platform: I can see the routing rule change at 02:05 that moved tenant-acme to priority pool low-cap. config id: route-tilt-202. That pool has per-worker concurrency cap = 32, old pool had 80.

jess_sre: That would explain queueing. If steady traffic remained same but cap lowered, admission controller will queue and then start failing. Did autoscaler scale the pool?

liz_runtime: Autoscaler didn't kick — pool marked as reserved and scale_policy=manual for that pool. No extra instances spun up. Worker CPU/GPU saturation is ~95% on shard-gpu-7.

raj_oncall: Repro steps (from support):
1) run: for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME_TOKEN>" -d '{"input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done
2) observe ~p99 latency > 2s and intermittent 503.

maria_support: customer attached small log snippet: ```
[02:13:01] req=req_0a9f3c queue_ms=1203 worker_wait=true result=503
[02:13:01] req=req_0a9f3d queue_ms=1188 worker_wait=true result=200
```

liz_runtime: quick mitigation options:
- roll back route-tilt-202 to previous pool (fastest)
- temporarily raise per-worker concurrency cap to 64 for priority pool (safe if perf OK)
- enable short-term burst nodes / scale up pool manually
Which do we want?

tom_platform: Rollback is lowest blast radius. I can flip route-tilt-202 back to route-prev at ~02:45 if y'all sign off.

jess_sre: Also recommend lowering admission queue timeout threshold to reduce 503s instead of long tail queuing — make those fail fast so SDKs can retry/backoff. But that doesn't fix capacity.

raj_oncall: Agreed. Immediate plan: 1) rollback routing -> restore to previous pool (tom) 2) increase admission timeout from 3s to 1.5s for that pool (liz/jess) 3) follow-up add autoscale policy for priority pool (tom).

tom_platform: Rolling back now. will post deploybot confirmation.

deploybot: deploy started: rollback route-tilt-202 -> route-prev (id: dpl-8812). initiating config update across edge nodes.

maria_support: telling customer we have a rollback in flight, ETA ~5m for global convergence. asking them to pause heavy replays. :pray:

deploybot: deploy succeeded: dpl-8812 applied. routing reverted at 02:49 UTC.

liz_runtime: post-rollback metrics: worker saturation down to ~55%, p99 latency back to baseline ~220ms, no 503s observed in last 2m. good.

jess_sre: Follow-ups: - schedule autoscale on that pool (policy: cpu/gpu 70% -> scale +2) - change per-worker concurrency plan to conservative 48 and run perf test - add a canary window for routing rule changes to move 5% traffic for 10m before full switch.

tom_platform: I'll open a platform ticket with exec plan and roll schedule.

maria_support: ACME updated: latency normalized, they stopped repro. Marking as customer-acknowledged. Thanks team.

raj_oncall: Root cause summary for postmortem: routing change moved tenant to smaller reserved pool without autoscale or capacity parity -> queueing under sustained load -> admission controller queued leading to long tail and 503s. Immediate rollback mitigated. Follow-ups as noted.

maria_support: I'll create the support ticket and close after follow-ups assigned. thread closed unless someone wants to add more. :white_check_mark:
